history.heading: The Trucial States
paragraphs: The United Arab Emirates lie on the southeastern coast of the Arabian Peninsula. The region has been inhabited for thousands of years, with Bronze Age sites such as Hili and links to ancient trade with Mesopotamia and the Indus Valley. Islam arrived in the 7th century.

The coastal sheikhdoms lived from pearl diving, fishing, trade and date farming. In the 19th century they signed truces with Britain, becoming known as the Trucial States, under British protection. The collapse of the pearl trade in the 1930s caused hardship.

history.heading: Federation and oil
paragraphs: Oil was discovered in Abu Dhabi in 1958. When Britain withdrew, six emirates formed the United Arab Emirates on 2 December 1971 under Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan of Abu Dhabi, the founding father; Ras Al Khaimah joined in 1972. Oil wealth transformed the country. In 2020 the UAE normalised relations with Israel through the Abraham Accords, and the same year it launched the Hope probe, the Arab world's first mission to Mars.

culture.heading: Tradition and globalisation
paragraphs: Arabic is the official language, and English is widely used. Emirati citizens are only about 10 percent of the population; most residents are expatriates from South Asia, the Arab world, the Philippines and the West. Islam is the state religion, and other faiths are permitted.

Traditions include falconry, camel racing, the al-ayyala dance, Arabic coffee and dates. Dubai's Burj Khalifa is the world's tallest building, and the Louvre Abu Dhabi and the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque are landmarks.

politics.heading: Federal monarchy
paragraphs: The UAE is a federation of seven absolute monarchies: Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, Ajman, Umm Al Quwain, Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah. The rulers form the Federal Supreme Council, which elects the president, traditionally the ruler of Abu Dhabi, Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed since 2022. The ruler of Dubai is vice-president and prime minister. Political parties are not allowed, and dissent is restricted.
The UAE has an assertive foreign policy and has been involved in conflicts in Yemen, Libya and Sudan.

economy.heading: Beyond oil
paragraphs: The UAE has one of the world's largest oil reserves, mostly in Abu Dhabi, and very large sovereign wealth funds. Dubai has diversified into trade, logistics (the port of Jebel Ali and Emirates airline), tourism, real estate and finance. The country is investing heavily in artificial intelligence, renewable and nuclear energy.
Income is high, and there is no personal income tax. The UAE hosted COP28 in 2023. The dirham is pegged to the US dollar.
